correctness.rationale: The explicit deficiency-two matching-to-derangement map and two possible swaps are bijective and exhaust the legal moves; resulting all-order degree, edge and sign formulas are algebraically reconstructed. The S_n conjugacy action has orbit parameters (k,lambda) and exactly the stated orbit sizes, so one BFS per orbit is an exhaustive proof of finite metric data. Two independent checkers enumerated all size-(n-1) crown matchings for 3 <= n <= 8, in distinct partial-injection versus derangement representations, checked reciprocal transitions, reached every state from each orbit representative, and produced byte-for-byte identical detailed distance outputs. There is no unproved infinite diameter claim.

evidence: An earlier complete-graph result concerns almost-perfect matchings in odd K_{2m+1}, with only one free vertex and no forbidden diagonal bipartite edges. Its distance formula uses alternating cycle counts; this is not the same graph or move system.

An earlier derangement-switch result allows swaps at any two positions. The present crown encoding restricts the swapped positions to 0 or its current inverse image of 0, so the earlier graph is strictly larger, e.g. at six symbols 1260 versus 840 edges.
General claw-free connectivity for nonmaximum independent sets is already known, so its application here is explicitly not new.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The available statements give either a different underlying graph or a supergraph with more moves. Graph distance in a supergraph is a lower bound, not an equality certificate, for this restricted subgraph. None implies the exact order-eight center, radius or 11-step antipodal count.

evidence: Direct bijection: matching with one free vertex per side corresponds to a derangement on n+1 points with distinguished 0; slides are only transpositions involving 0 or its preimage, so this is a strict spanning subgraph of the graph allowing arbitrary valid transpositions.

For n=5 the target graph has 265 states and 840 edges; the broader all-position derangement-swap graph on six symbols has 265 states and 1260 edges. Identical state counts alone do not imply identical distances.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The derangement relabeling is handled as a genuine equivalence, not hidden behind distinct terminology. Generic full-swap metrics and other matching-exchange operations cannot supply the exact restricted-slide distance census without an additional, unlocated equivalence theorem.

originality.rationale: The claimed novelty is the exact finite token-slide metric through eight crown sizes, including the parity-dependent eccentricity split and the 133,496-state, 2,593,920-antipodal-pair order-eight census. Generic connectivity, all-order derangement enumeration and signed imbalance are explicitly credited and not treated as sufficient novelty. Source comparisons inspected the most relevant primary sections; no covering theorem was found, but possible unindexed exact tables are a material residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed published or archived computation could give an identical finite crown matching-slide distance table, or a stronger general result could imply the table.
The finite data establish no diameter or centrality law for n >= 9; continuing the observed parity pattern is conjectural.
Model conventions in other reconfiguration papers vary between token jumping and token sliding and require care when comparing implications.

value.rationale: The exact radius, diameter, eccentricity partition and full all-pairs distances are natural reachability invariants of matching slides on standard crown graphs. The finite census has 133,496 vertices, 15 symmetry orbits and 2,593,920 antipodal unordered pairs at n=8, going materially beyond counting or generic connectivity. The parity-controlled centrality split from n=3 through n=8 is structural, constrains hypotheses for larger n, and supplies a reproducible benchmark. The all-order count and elementary sign obstruction are contextual, not the sole significance justification.
